title: Mount drivers: a coordinates request refused before BUSY is published does not keep its ALERT
description: indigo_update_coordinates() keeps a MOUNT_EQUATORIAL_COORDINATES ALERT only when it follows a published BUSY. Refusals that never publish BUSY are therefore overwritten by the next poll: the generator's parked-mount guard, mount_rainbow while homing, mount_lx200 classic guiding. The Mount Agent can then read the following OK as a successful sync or slew. Deliberately left out of step 2 of ticket 42b85be0 by the owner's decision. Needs a design decision (base library and possibly generator; both need the owner's approval of the concrete change). Found while working on ticket 42b85be0-1f19-4607-b3c3-746e60317d17 (closed, commit a09e0f878), which introduced the kept coordinates ALERT in indigo_update_coordinates(): an ALERT published after a BUSY stays until the next BUSY. Reproduce in the driver's simulator suite before changing code.

outcome.summary:
Independent review of git diff master...HEAD at 824f8f7fd.

BLOCKING
1. indigo_test/integration/mount_coordinates_test_common.h:83-86,125-128 - hold_coordinates_queue() can queue its gate on a freed device from an earlier test case. coordinates_queue_device is cleared only when start_coordinates_publications() gets a different device name, and stop_coordinates_publications() removes the hook, so publications from a later driver instance with the same name never refresh it. starbook_request_behind_park_is_refused_and_kept (test_mount_starbook_simulator.c:1986-1987) and temma_request_behind_park_is_refused_and_kept (test_mount_temma_simulator.c:2067-2068) call start_coordinates_publications() and then hold_coordinates_queue() right away, so they pick up the pointer stored by the earlier *_coordinates_publish_the_mount_position case. That device was freed when the earlier case shut the driver down (indigo_safe_free in INDIGO_DRIVER_SHUTDOWN), so indigo_execute_handler() then runs on freed memory. Evidence: a scratch copy of the header that logs the pointer shows, in both suites, that the pointer from the earlier case is the one hold uses ('PTRDBG hold uses 0x7a7b050700' for starbook, '0x7af1520000' for temma), and no later publication reports a different device. The cases pass only because the allocator happens to give the new device the same address. Under ASan (quarantine), on another allocator or with another case order the gate holds a dead queue, or crashes, and the case becomes flaky or vacuous. Fix: clear coordinates_queue_device on every start_coordinates_publications() (or in stop_coordinates_publications()) and let hold wait for the next publication. Its loop already waits up to 5 s, and forced updates make the next poll publish.

NON-BLOCKING
2. indigo_libs/indigo_mount_driver.c:1432 -> 1413 - indigo_reject_coordinates_change() formats its arguments into message, then update_coordinates() passes that string to indigo_update_property() as a format. A '%' in t

3. test_mount_synscan_simulator.c: the added blank line before cleanup: is removed.

New unit case coordinates_message_is_published_as_text: it fails without the fix and passes with it. With the fix all 8 cases pass. It is not vacuous: it compares the exact text the client receives.

Q2 accepted: the kept ALERT of MOUNT_EQUATORIAL_COORDINATES and MOUNT_HORIZONTAL_COORDINATES lasts through unpark until the next request or motion. Q3 failures after BUSY that bypass indigo_update_coordinates() stay in the separate tickets 3beb3554 (synscan), 0923e7a5 (nexstaraux), e2e60912 (pmc8); do not fix them here. Q4 include the base-class sync refusal fix (indigo_mount_driver.c:811-812). Q5 mount_asi and mount_mxhd stay untouched. Q6 one change commit with the generator change and all ten regenerated drivers. Q7 final recorded runs are non-interactive simulator runs of the ten mount drivers and agent_mount. Nothing beyond these diffs is approved for the library or the generator.
Running affected mount suites, agent_mount, unit and generator tests (unrecorded)

Implementer reproduction record (2026-11-20). Red: the new/extended refusal cases were built against a git-archive copy of HEAD (old library, generator output and drivers) with the new test sources and all failed: mount_simulator mount_park_home_and_parked_guards, synscan keeps_state_when_parked_request_is_refused and goto_admitted_during_homing_is_refused, rainbow park_slews_to_park_position, refuses_motion_while_searching_for_home and goto_admitted_before_a_park_is_refused, starbook request_behind_park_is_refused_and_kept, temma request_behind_park_is_refused_and_kept, pmc8 park_replaces_a_goto_and_guards_the_parked_mount, nexstar park_guards_and_unpark, nexstaraux parked_guards, ioptron park_workflow_8407, lx200 park_rejects_motion_and_unpark_recovers and classic_guiding_refusal_is_published (old refusals are published without MOUNT_HORIZONTAL_COORDINATES and the next poll publishes OK; pmc8/nexstaraux/ioptron/simulator keep the ALERT by accident, they fail on the missing horizontal publication). Unit cases coordinates_refusal_is_kept_until_busy and reject_macro_on_busy_only_sends_message fail with the refusal term of the state machine removed; the generator architecture case fails with the old generator. Green: all pass with the change. Deviation found: the approved Q4 diff (section 5.1, update_coordinates(device, !synced, NULL) at indigo_mount_driver.c:811) makes an accepted base-class sync after a refused one publish ALERT (existing unit case sync_near_the_pole_is_refused fails: expected OK, got ALERT), because that path publishes no BUSY; the Q4 hunk is not applied, owner decision needed.

Q4 of the design (base-class sync refusal, indigo_mount_driver.c:811-812): the approved hunk update_coordinates(device, !synced, NULL) is wrong. That path never publishes BUSY, so after a refused sync the kept flag makes the next accepted sync publish ALERT (unit case sync_near_the_pole_is_refused fails: expected 1, got 3). It was not applied. Options: (a) leave lines 811-812 unchanged in this ticket; no generated driver reaches this path; (b) add a third mode 'accepted request' to the private update_coordinates() that clears the flag like BUSY, line 811 becomes update_coordinates(device, synced ? accepted : refusal, NULL). Which one?
Merging master into the ticket branch
Rerunning merged suites (unit, generator, pmc8, temma, nexstar, ioptron, nexstaraux, starbook, agent_mount)
Owner decision 2026-11-20: option (a). Leave indigo_mount_driver.c:811-812 (base-class sync refusal) unchanged in this ticket; the Q4 hunk of design section 5.1 is dropped and no third mode is added.
Library, generator and driver diffs read; reviewing tests
Checking stale device pointer in hold_coordinates_queue with a scratch starbook build

Approve the one-line change: publish with the format "%s" and the text as argument when a message is present?

Owner: yes, publish the refusal message with format "%s" and the text as argument in update_coordinates() (indigo_mount_driver.c).

3. indigo_test/integration/test_mount_synscan_simulator.c:438 - the added block brings one more blank line inside synscan_mount_keeps_state_when_parked_request_is_refused. The function already had blank lines on master. Formatting rule only.

VERIFIED
- Library: matches 5.1 apart from the Q4 hunk; indigo_mount_driver.c:811-812 is unchanged and there is no third mode. The keep flag is still written only in update_coordinates() and on disconnect. Behavior per state: idle OK publishes ALERT and keeps it; a kept ALERT stays kept; on a BUSY property the function itself (handler guard B1) sets ALERT and keeps it; with the property BUSY the macro sends the message only through indigo_reject_change(), changes nothing and returns INDIGO_OK; a hidden horizontal property is skipped; disconnect clears the flag. The header doc is accurate; no existing ABI changes. The bus-thread vs poll race is of the same kind as the existing indigo_reject_change() and the copy macros.
- Generator: diff equals 5.2. I built the master and worktree generators in scratch and regenerated all 119 parseable .driver files. Every checked-in .c/.h/_main.c is byte-identical to the new generator's output. Old and new generator output differ only in the ten mount drivers, and only in the MOUNT_EQUATORIAL_COORDINATES guard and reject lines: 10 admission, 10 handler, 2 rainbow reject_change. MOUNT_MOTION_* and MOUNT_TRACKING are unchanged, as are all non-mount drivers.
- Drivers: each diff holds only the guard lines, the lx200 classic-guiding refusal, the synscan 'Mount is moving' refusal, the rainbow reject_change lines and the version. Every version is master+1. Master's merged fixes are intact, because nothing else differs. No changes in README.md, TEST_SUMMARY.md, the Xcode project or the off-limits drivers.
- Bus/agent: refusals publish one ALERT with the message, values at the position, targets unchanged, HORIZONTAL ALERT too, no BUSY. The ALERT is kept until the next BUSY. Mount Agent (indigo_agent_mount.c:436-512): a kept ALERT makes the final state non-OK, so the result is a failure instead of 'Synced'.
- Deviations B2/A3: sound. A real classic LX200 moves at RG and its generic poll needs >2' per poll to report slewing, so the refusal is kept there. A rainbow pulse is real motion (:CL1#), and a BUSY from that motion ends the ALERT by the approved rule. The lx200 3-attempt retry only skips attempts where the request was never admitted (no BUSY with its target), so it hides nothing.
- Counts in MIGRATION_STATUS.md equal the registered cases (lx200 168 incl. --tcp, rainbow 42, starbook 29, synscan 107, temma 33); Comment column untouched. Docs are accurate English and make no base-class sync claim.
- Runs (scratch builds against the worktree build products): starbook and temma full suites pass; rainbow full suite passes (one case failed only because the scratch cwd lacked fixtures/, and passes when they are present); lx200 classic_guiding_refusal_is_published and park_rejects_motion_and_unpark_recovers pass. questions.text: Q4 of the design (base-class sync refusal, indigo_mount_driver.c:811-812): the approved hunk update_coordinates(device, !synced, NULL) is wrong. That path never publishes BUSY, so after a refused sync the kept flag makes the next accepted sync publish ALERT (unit case sync_near_the_pole_is_refused fails: expected 1, got 3). It was not applied. Options: (a) leave lines 811-812 unchanged in this ticket; no generated driver reaches this path; (b) add a third mode 'accepted request' to the private update_coordinates() that clears the flag like BUSY, line 811 becomes update_coordinates(device, synced ? accepted : refusal, NULL). Which one?
questions.answer: Owner decision 2026-11-20: option (a). Leave indigo_mount_driver.c:811-812 (base-class sync refusal) unchanged in this ticket; the Q4 hunk of design section 5.1 is dropped and no third mode is added.

questions.text: Review finding in the approved library diff: indigo_reject_coordinates_change() formats its message and update_coordinates() then passes the formatted text to indigo_update_property() as a format string (indigo_mount_driver.c:1432 -> :1413). A '%' in a refusal reason would be interpreted a second time. No current caller passes one. Approve the one-line change: publish with the format "%s" and the text as argument when a message is present?
questions.answer: Owner: yes, publish the refusal message with format "%s" and the text as argument in update_coordinates() (indigo_mount_driver.c).
